result.title: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
result.comment: 21 pages of main text (including references), with 4 figures and 3 tables, plus 16 pages of appendices
result.summary: We study context-aware time-series forecasting, in which a single target variable is predicted from its own history and a set of contextual variables, such as weather and calendar information. As the context becomes more diverse, a single model struggles to capture all of its regimes, while ensemble learning and Mixture-of-Experts approaches rely on manual data partitioning or soft routing, which increases the inference cost and hinders interpretability. We propose CATF, a Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting framework built on a Manager-Worker architecture: a Transformer-based Manager routes each input to a single Worker based on the context, using hard routing during both training and inference. The Workers thus specialize without manual data partitioning, and any single-model forecaster can serve as a Worker. On five context-rich datasets, four horizons, and two normalization schemes, CATF improves over its standalone counterpart in 162 of 200 comparisons, the best CATF-enhanced model outperforms the best standalone baseline in 19 of 20 settings, and it outperforms the zero-shot Time-MoE foundation model in 15 of 20 settings. A case study on bike-sharing data shows that the Manager routes inputs by the calendar and that each Worker specializes in a different weekly pattern.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CATF：由 Transformer Manager 根据上下文将输入硬路由到单个专职 Worker，实现无需人工划分数据的时序预测专家分工，并在多个上下文丰富的数据集与预测步长上优于单体模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作关注按上下文把输入分派给专职子模型，与 LVR 中多 latent 假设、并行推理路径的计算分配与可解释路由问题可能有概念联系，可供核查其硬路由训练与专家专门化是否可类比到推理期路径选择；但研究领域为时序预测，迁移性尚不确定。
